name: Cessna 150/152
summary: Small two-seat high-wing trainer built in huge numbers from 1958 to 1985; still one of the most common primary trainers and rental aircraft in the US.

wings: Strut-braced high wing, one lift strut per side
Constant-chord inner wing with tapered outer panels
Short span relative to four-seat look-alikes
engines: Single small flat-four in a short, narrow cowling
Two-blade fixed-pitch propeller with small spinner
fuselage: Tiny two-seat side-by-side cabin with a door each side
Fixed tricycle gear with spring-steel main legs
Short, stubby fuselage; nose wheel looks large for the airframe
tail: Swept fin with dorsal fillet on 1966+ models, straight fin on early ones

tellTales: Strut-braced high wing over a very small two-seat cabin
Short, stubby proportions — clearly smaller than four-seat high-wings
Fixed tricycle gear on spring-steel legs

confusedWith.howToTell: The 150/152 is visibly smaller and stubbier with a two-seat cabin; the 172 has a longer four-seat cabin and longer wing.
The DA20 is a low-wing composite with a T-tail and bubble canopy; the 150/152 is a strut-braced metal high-wing with a low tail.
The Luscombe is a taildragger; the 150/152 sits on tricycle gear.

usCount.source: FAA Aircraft Registry make/model query (registered aircraft): ~8,200 Cessna 150 + ~1,700 Cessna 152
